# Dashes and semicolons

## Dashes that enclose a clause

A pair of dashes around a clause with a verb of its own is left for a person to reword.

The cache — which is rebuilt every night — stays small.

The cache — which was rebuilt last night — stays small.

The caches — which were rebuilt last night — stay small.

The caches — which are rebuilt every night — stay small.

The cache — and I am sure of this — stays small.

The cache — which has grown lately — stays small.

The caches — which have grown lately — stay small.

The cache — which had grown last year — stayed small.

The cache — which will grow over time — stays small.

The cache — which would grow without limits — stays small.

The cache — which could grow without limits — stays small.

The cache — which should be pruned weekly — stays small.

The cache — which can grow without limits — stays small.

The cache — which may grow over time — stays small.

The cache — which might grow over time — stays small.

The cache — which must be pruned weekly — stays small.

The cache — which does grow over time — stays small.

The caches — which do grow over time — stay small.

The cache — which did grow last year — stayed small.

A pair of dashes around a short phrase becomes a pair of commas.

The cache, a single file on disk, stays small.

## Single dashes

A dash between two clauses becomes a period and a new sentence, whichever form of dash it is.

The form stays clean.
Save is disabled until an edit.

The form stays clean.
Save is disabled until an edit.

The form stays clean.
Save is disabled until an edit.

## Words that stay lowercase

A word that is always written in lowercase cannot start a sentence, so the dash before it becomes a colon.

The runner: npm handles the install step.

The runner: git fetches the sources.

The runner: cargo builds the crates.

The runner: pip installs the wheels.

The runner: rustc compiles the build script.

The runner: rustfmt checks the formatting.

The runner: clippy lints the sources.

The runner: ffmpeg encodes the preview.

The runner: ffprobe reads the metadata.

The runner: npx starts the local server.

The runner: yarn installs the workspace.

The runner: pnpm installs the workspace.

The runner: brew installs the tools.

The runner: apt installs the packages.

The runner: curl downloads the archive.

The runner: wget mirrors the site.

The runner: ssh opens the tunnel.

The runner: sudo installs the service.

The runner: bash runs the setup script.

The runner: zsh loads the profile.

The runner: sh runs the portable script.

The runner: docker builds the image.

The runner: kubectl applies the manifests.

The runner: iOS builds need a signing key.

The runner: macOS builds need a notarized binary.

## Semicolons and colons

A semicolon between two clauses becomes a period and a new sentence.

The cache is small.
It is rebuilt every night.

An introduction of several words that ends in a colon gets a line of its own when the text after it is long.

Skip objects without a hierarchy path:
they share every other field with a sibling but have no way to tell themselves apart from it.
